summary: Michael Torsten Much specializes in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Ernst Steinkellner and served as a fellow at the University of Hamburg.

Michael Viggo Fausbøll (1821–1908) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Cand.theol. at the University of Copenhagen (1838–1847), studying under Niels Ludvig Westergaard. He served Copenhagen as assistant librarian (1861) and Professor of Indian Philology (1878–1902).

Michael W. Meister is a history, archaeology, and Indology scholar. He studied at Harvard (B.A. ~1960–1964; M.A. ~1968–1971; Ph.D. ~1971–1974) and the University of Pennsylvania, where he became a professor around 1976.

Michael Weiers (1937–2025) was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He completed his dissertation at the University of Bonn in 1965, later serving there as professor (1972–2003) and as an honorary professor at Inner Mongolia University.

Michael Wenger is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He completed an M.A. at The New School and studied under Sojun Mel Weitsman. He served as Dean of Buddhist Studies at San Francisco Zen Center (~1984) and guiding teacher at Dragons Leap (~2012).

Michael Willis is an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. He earned a B.A. from the University of Victoria under Siri Gunasinghe and Alan Gowans, and a 1988 doctorate from the University of Chicago under J. A. B. van Buitenen and Pramod Chandra, later curating at the British Museum (1994–2014).

Michael Witzel is an Indologist and linguist. He studied under Hoffmann, Thieme, Schmidt, Narten, Kuiper, and Pandit. He led the Nepal Research Centre and preservation project (1972–1978), held the Sanskrit chair at Leiden (1978–1986), and joined Harvard in 1986.

Michael Zimmermann works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Hamburg (Ph.D. ~1993–2000 under Schmithausen), Soka University, and IRIAB. He held posts at Stanford (2003), Nepal Research Centre (2002), and Hamburg (director ~2007).

Michael von Brück is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his doctorate at the University of Rostock (1968–1973) and held professorships at the University of Regensburg (1988–1991) and the University of Munich (~1991–2014).

Michaela Haas is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Bonn under doctoral supervisor Peter Schwieger and also studied under Jigme Namgyal and Rechungpa.

Michaela Mross specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. She studied at Komazawa University and completed her PhD at the University of Munich in 2014. Her posts include a postdoctoral fellowship at UC Berkeley and assistant professorship at Stanford University (attested 2017).

Michaël Peyrot specializes in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at Leiden University (1999–2010), holding posts there (~2008, 2016) and at the Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences and Humanities (2014–2016).

Michel Bréal (1832–1915) worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at ENS, University of Berlin, and under Bopp and Weber. His posts included the Bibliothèque nationale, professor at Collège de France (1864–1905), and director at EPHE (~1868–1905).

Michel Clasquin-Johnson is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He completed his undergraduate and graduate education, including his doctoral thesis, at the University of South Africa, where he also took up a post in 1990.

Michel Hulin (1936–2026) was a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure (1956) and under Olivier Lacombe at Paris-Sorbonne University (~1970–1977), where he later served on the faculty from 1981 to 1998.

Michel Jacq-Hergoualc'h (1943–2014) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Jean Boisselier in 1988 and served as a professor at Sorbonne Nouvelle University from around 1993 to 2008.

Michel Lejeune (1907–2000) was a French linguist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure (~1926–1929) and under Antoine Meillet (~1926–1932). He held academic posts at the University of Poitiers (~1937–1941), the University of Paris (~1946–1977), and the EPHE (~1947–1977).

Michel Mohr specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Geneva and studied under Seizan Yanagida. His posts include the University of Geneva (1987–1992), Hanazono University (attested 2000–2006), and the University of Hawaiʻi (attested 2008–2012).

Michel Soymié (1924–2002) worked in Sinology and Buddhist studies after studying at INALCO (~1948–1952). He held posts at CNRS, Maison Franco-Japonaise, EFEO, and served as Chair of History and Philosophy of Mediaeval China at EPHE (~1966–1992).

Michel Strickmann (1942–1994) worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at EPHE and Paris Diderot, trained under Hulsewé, Zürcher, Vos, Kaltenmark, Stein, Vandermeersch, Schipper, and Okumura, and held posts at Bordeaux, UC Berkeley, and Wissenschaftskolleg zu Berlin.
